requirements.text: A claim of this profile MUST identify the AARM revision it implements by the version, revisions and digests that this profile pins, and MUST declare, for each in-scope action class, whether the AARM control plane implements the ECL Decision Layer for that class or supplies `judgment` inputs to a separate ECL Decision Layer.

When the AARM control plane implements the Decision Layer, it MUST answer each DCMP-2 decision request with a DCMP-2 decision response that binds the exact request (DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-051) and is signed under the claim's trust policy with a key that the policy accepts for the decision-response purpose (TRUST-POLICY-1), and an enforcement point MUST release an action only on such a response; an AARM decision, receipt or other AARM artifact MUST NOT release an action by itself. A retained exchange record's `response` and each retained `modification_response` MUST bind the record's corresponding `request` or `modification_request` under DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-050, with the reference profile's response clock-skew allowance of zero, whether or not the action was released and for every outcome. The authority checks that those requirements restrict to `admit` apply only to `admit`. A record verifier MUST report a missing corresponding request or a failed response binding with `ecl.error.request-binding-invalid.v1`, retaining the underlying binding failure's code in the diagnostic message.

The ECL outcome for an action that an AARM decision governs MUST be at least as strict, in the strictness order of the core standard (Section 4.3), as the outcome this mapping gives: ALLOW maps to `admit` only when policy evaluated over `verifiable` inputs permits the action under the one-way rule of the core standard (Section 5.2), and otherwise to `deny`; DENY maps to `deny`; STEP_UP maps to `challenge` naming the approval required (ECL1N-0174, ECL1N-0177), or to `hold`; DEFER maps to `hold`; MODIFY maps to `deny` of the original request, with the modified action handled under AB1-004.

A MODIFY decision MUST NOT release the original action. The modified action, if it is to go ahead, MUST be submitted as a new DCMP-2 decision request that carries the modified parameters as the same JSON values in `action.parameters`, and their digest in `action.parameters_digest`, carries the original request's `issuer`, `actor`, `subject`, `delegation_chain`, `authority_request`, `constraints` and `integrity_policy`, and its `action` with only `action_id`, `parameters` and `parameters_digest` changed, names the original request as a causal predecessor by identifier and digest with the relation `ecl.relation.modification-of.v1`, and is evaluated and admitted on its own; an enforcement point MUST release only the parameters that the new request's `admit` binds. A MODIFY whose modified parameters change the action's target or operation, as the deployment derives them from the parameters, MUST end in `deny` of the original with no new request. An exchange record of a MODIFY that holds neither a `modification_request` nor a `release` records a `deny` of the original with no new request and MUST NOT be reported for the missing new request, since the record does not show why the modified action did not go ahead; one that holds a `modification_response` without its `modification_request` MUST be reported as `ecl.rule.aarm-modification-new-request.v1`. A decision other than MODIFY has no new request: the enforcement point MUST release the action, if at all, only on the `admit` of the original request, and an exchange record whose `aarm_decision` is not MODIFY and that holds a `modification_request` or a `modification_response` MUST be reported as `ecl.rule.aarm-modification-new-request.v1`.

A `hold` or `challenge` mapped from DEFER or STEP_UP MUST carry an `expires_at` no later than the deadline of the deferral or approval, and a `safe_state` under which the waiting action is not released: `ecl.state.fail-closed.v1`, `ecl.state.quarantine.v1`, `ecl.state.emergency-halt.v1` or `ecl.state.restricted.v1`. The expiry of that deadline, or the AARM control plane's failure to answer within its declared timeout, MUST end in an outcome that releases nothing (DCMP2-018, DCMP2-041).

The outputs of AARM R2 (context accumulation, including the data classifications it records), R3 (policy evaluation with intent alignment, including any confidence score) and R7 (semantic distance), and in the judgment-source role every AARM output including the AARM decision itself (R4), MUST be treated as `judgment` inputs: the Consequential Action Register MUST declare each of them `judgment`; the exchange record MUST list each one that the decision consulted in `inputs` with that class and its `aarm_requirement`, and the decision response MUST record it in `ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1` with that class (AB1-013); each of them MUST NOT be part of the basis of an `admit`, and an `admit` MUST rest on `verifiable` inputs only. An AARM DENY, STEP_UP or DEFER that rests on them MAY make the outcome stricter. In the judgment-source role, the inputs MUST include exactly one input whose `aarm_requirement` is `R4`, of class `judgment`. These classes hold in every decision basis that the exchange record holds: an entry of the `ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1` of the record's `modification_response` whose `input` is an input that the record lists with an `aarm_requirement` that this requirement makes `judgment` MUST have the class `judgment`.

Each AARM receipt for an in-scope action MUST be bound to the ECL evidence of that action: the action's `execution_terminal` event MUST carry the registered extension `ecl.ext.aarm-receipt.v1` with the receipt's identifier (its `receipt_id`), the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the RFC 8785 canonical form of the receipt as retained, signature included, and the AARM decision that the receipt records in `decision.result`; that decision MUST be the decision the exchange record holds and consistent with the ECL outcome under AB1-003, and the receipt's `action.parameters` MUST have, under DCMP2-007, the digest that the decision request carries in `action.parameters_digest`. The record's `terminal` member MUST be an `execution_terminal` event with an execution payload and a terminal execution state, and MUST satisfy the applicable EBMP-2 object semantic rules. A record verifier MUST reject a nonterminal event in this member. The record API checks the action identifier, receipt binding and response-independent terminal outcome-reason clauses of EBMP2-056; terminal-to-response decision references, causal closure and signatures remain checks of signed-bundle verification under EBMP-2.

The signed ECL evidence bundle MUST be treated as the record of whether an action was authorized and released (EBMP2-045): an AARM receipt supports claims about the AARM evaluation, such as the context it accumulated, the intent alignment it computed, the policy it matched and its reasons, and MUST NOT be used to establish that an action was authorized or released; a receipt that disagrees with the ECL evidence MUST be reported as a verification finding, and the ECL evidence governs.

An adapter that retains exchange records for this profile MUST write each one as `ecl_aarm_exchange_v1`, valid against `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/binding/aarm-exchange/1`, and every value of `ecl.ext.aarm-receipt.v1` it emits MUST validate against `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/extension/aarm-receipt/1`.

The modification request MUST be decided under the register version of the first decision. If that version is no longer in force, the Decision Layer MUST NOT admit the modification.

requirements.text: An ACS hook point MUST NOT be claimed as an ECL enforcement point unless the governed AI system can neither bypass it, disable it nor change the decision it applies (ECL1N-0033, ECL1N-0043, ECL1N-0046), and the Consequential Action Register records its enforcement class with its rationale and residual bypass risk (ECL1N-0044, ECL1N-0045). A hook point that runs in a process, container or account in which the governed AI system can execute code, or that the governed AI system can start, stop or reconfigure, MUST NOT be claimed as an ECL enforcement point; it MAY carry the Guardian's decision to an ECL decision point, where AC1-004 gives that decision its class and the decision is not a `verifiable` input unless the decision point verifies the Guardian's signature over it under a key that the governed AI system cannot use.

A Guardian decision MUST reach an ECL enforcement point only through a DCMP-2 decision response that an ECL decision point issues and signs for the exact request (DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-051); an enforcement point MUST release an action only on that response's `admit`, and a Guardian `allow` MUST NOT create, widen or extend ECL authority, so the decision point still applies its native authority, scope, validity, budget and human-approval checks. A retained exchange record's `response` and each retained `modification_response` MUST bind the record's corresponding `request` or `modification_request` under DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-050, with the reference profile's response clock-skew allowance of zero, whether or not the action was released and for every outcome. The authority checks that those requirements restrict to `admit` apply only to `admit`. A record verifier MUST report a missing corresponding request or a failed response binding with `ecl.error.request-binding-invalid.v1`, retaining the underlying binding failure's code in the diagnostic message.

The ECL outcome for an action that a Guardian decision governs MUST be at least as strict, in the strictness order of the core standard (Section 4.3), as the outcome this mapping gives: `allow` maps to `admit` only when policy evaluated over `verifiable` inputs permits the action under the one-way rule of the core standard (Section 5.2), and otherwise to `deny`; `deny` maps to `deny`; `ask` maps to `challenge` naming the approval required (ECL1N-0174, ECL1N-0177), or to `hold` or `deny` where the Guardian substitutes for an approver-incapable client; `defer` maps to `hold` carrying the resolution condition and deadline (DCMP2-018); `modify` maps to `deny` of the original request, with the modified action handled under AC1-005. A Guardian decision whose evaluator is `agent` or `composite`, or that states no evaluator, is a `judgment` input. Any other Guardian decision is `actor_supplied` when it reaches the ECL decision point through a hook point or any other channel that the governed AI system can write, unless the decision point verifies the Guardian's signature over the decision under a key that the governed AI system cannot use, authenticates a commitment to the exact evaluated ACS request params, and checks the authenticated session, hooked-step identifier and method against the current request; an ACS-Core HMAC under a key that the Observed Agent holds does not qualify, and an ACS-Crypto asymmetric signature under a key held only by the Guardian qualifies only with that request-content and context binding (ECL1N-0178, AC1-009). The request commitment MUST be obtained from a verified ACS chain whose signed head commits to a step `request_hash`, or from a directly authenticated request digest under a declared signed representation. Matching a `request_id` alone is insufficient. The decision point MUST compare the commitment with the exact request it submitted for the current step and check the mapping of those params to the actual DCMP request. Otherwise it takes the least trusted class of the inputs it evaluated, so one that evaluated SessionContext, Intent or other content the governed AI system wrote is `actor_supplied`. A Guardian decision that is a `judgment` or `actor_supplied` input MAY make the outcome stricter and MUST NOT be the basis of an `admit`. The exchange record MUST state in `guardian.channel` whether the decision point obtained the decision from the Guardian directly (`direct`), verified a Guardian signature under a key that the governed AI system cannot use (`signed`), or received it through a hook point (`hook`), and MUST name, in the `derived_from` of the Guardian decision's input, each decision input that the Guardian's request carried other than the action itself. Every decided Guardian input MUST explicitly carry `derived_from`, including an empty list when there were no other decision inputs, independently of its class. A missing list MUST be rejected with `ecl.rule.acs-judgment-guardian.v1`; it MUST NOT be inferred from a declared class. An unavailable Guardian decision after a failed exchange is recorded as unavailable, without inventing its evaluated inputs. A Guardian decision whose channel is `hook` MUST NOT be declared `verifiable`. When the response carries `ecl.ext.acs-decision.v1`, exactly one input MUST carry `guardian: true`. The class that this requirement gives a Guardian decision holds in every decision basis that the exchange record holds: an entry of the `ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1` of the record's `modification_response` whose `input` is the input that the record marks `guardian` MUST have the class of the marked input. When `guardian.channel` is `signed` and `guardian.status` is `decided`, the record MUST also give, in `guardian.key_id`, the identifier of the key under which the decision point verified the Guardian's signature and, in `guardian.request_params`, the exact ACS request envelope `params`. The `guardian.request_digest` MUST be the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the UTF-8 RFC 8785 canonical form of those params, excluding the outer envelope and signature. This is the hashing domain of ACS `ContextEntry.request_hash`, not the entire ACS envelope or DCMP message. The record MUST carry `guardian.authenticated_context` with the authenticated `session_id`, `request_id`, `method` and `request_digest`, matching the record's session, Guardian result's step identifier, hook and params digest. Its `dcmp_request_digest` MUST equal the SHA-256 digest of the RFC 8785 form of the record's DCMP `request`; it records the adapter's checked mapping to that request and is not itself claimed to be a field signed by the Guardian. A supplied chain for a decided signed exchange MUST include the step's `request_hash` equal to the params digest. A record verifier MUST reject a mismatch with `ecl.rule.acs-decision-recorded.v1`. On a failed exchange, `guardian.channel` names the attempted route, not a verified decision. For a failed signed route, `guardian.request_params` and `guardian.request_digest` MAY be omitted together; if either is retained, both MUST be retained and the digest MUST match the RFC 8785 form of those submitted params. Any retained `guardian.key_id` or `guardian.authenticated_context` is attempted or unavailable evidence, not a claim of successful authentication, and the record verifier MUST NOT require it to bind an unavailable Guardian result. These failed records remain subject to the deny and non-release requirements of AC1-006.

A `modify` decision MUST NOT release the original action. The action that the modification produces, if it is to go ahead, MUST be submitted as a new DCMP-2 decision request that carries the effective parameters after the modification as the same JSON values in `action.parameters`, and their digest in `action.parameters_digest`, carries the original request's `issuer`, `actor`, `subject`, `delegation_chain`, `authority_request`, `constraints` and `integrity_policy`, and its `action` with only `action_id`, `parameters` and `parameters_digest` changed, names the original request as a causal predecessor by identifier and digest with the relation `ecl.relation.modification-of.v1`, and is evaluated and admitted on its own; an enforcement point MUST release only the parameters that the new request's `admit` binds, and a `modifications` object that the pinned text forbids (a wholesale replacement combined with edits, or a redaction whose target overlaps a parameter override), or one that cannot be applied under the next section, MUST end in `deny` of the original with no new request. An exchange record of a `modify` that holds neither a `modification_request` nor a `release` records a `deny` of the original with no new request and MUST NOT be reported for the missing new request, since the record does not show why the modified action did not go ahead; one that holds a `modification_response` without its `modification_request` MUST be reported as `ecl.rule.acs-modification-new-request.v1`. A decision other than `modify`, and a decision failure, has no new request: the enforcement point MUST release the action, if at all, only on the `admit` of the original request, and an exchange record that records a decision failure, or a Guardian decision other than `modify`, and that holds a `modification_request` or a `modification_response` MUST be reported as `ecl.rule.acs-modification-new-request.v1`.

At an ECL enforcement point, a decision failure MUST end in the declared safe state and MUST NOT release the action, whatever `on_decision_failure` posture the handshake negotiated. A decision failure is any of these: no usable Guardian decision within the negotiated timeout; a transport failure; an error response without a decision; a decision whose disposition the mapping of AC1-004 does not name; a decision for a `request_id` other than the hooked step's; a response whose ACS signature, where the session requires one, does not verify; a signed-channel response whose request-content commitment, session, method or step does not match under AC1-004; and a decision that arrives after the enforcement point applied the safe state for the step. A deployment that claims this profile MUST negotiate `on_decision_failure` as `deny`, and MUST configure the startup posture that the pinned text sets out of band as `refuse`, so that a failed handshake starts no unguarded session for an in-scope action class.

The expiry of an `ask` or a `defer` MUST NOT release an in-scope action, even when the `ask` declares a `timeout_disposition` of `allow` or the `defer` a `timeout_decision` of `ask`: the ECL response for it MUST carry an `expires_at` no later than the Guardian's deadline and a `safe_state` under which the waiting action is not released (`ecl.state.fail-closed.v1`, `ecl.state.quarantine.v1`, `ecl.state.emergency-halt.v1` or `ecl.state.restricted.v1`), and the enforcement point MUST record the expiry as a non-release outcome. The Guardian's deadline is the instant at which the ECL deployment received the Guardian's decision, which the exchange record holds as `guardian.observed_at`, plus the `ask_details.timeout_seconds` of an `ask`, in seconds, or plus the `defer_details.resolution_timeout_ms` of a `defer`, in milliseconds (the pinned `ask-details.json` and `defer-details.json`).

For each Guardian decision that an ECL decision depends on, the ECL decision response MUST carry the registered extension `ecl.ext.acs-decision.v1` with the Guardian's decision, its evaluator, the ACS `request_id`, the `chain_hash` that the Guardian published for the step, and for a `modify` the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the RFC 8785 form of its `modifications` object; when the deployment claims the ACS-Audit profile, or supplies an ACS chain as the request-content commitment for a signed channel, it MUST also carry the step's `request_hash`, computed from the exact ACS request params as AC1-004 specifies. A verifier that recomputes the ACS session chain under the chain-hashing rule below MUST find each recorded `chain_hash` as the head after that step's ContextEntry, which is the entry whose `step_id` is the recorded `request_id`.

The chain-hashing rule restates section 8.2 of the pinned Instrument specification. A ContextEntry's `entry_hash` is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the RFC 8785 canonical form of the entry with its `entry_hash` and `previous_hash` members removed, followed by the 32 bytes that the entry's `previous_hash` encodes in hexadecimal, or by no bytes for the first entry of a session, whose `previous_hash` is null or absent. Each later entry's `previous_hash` is the `entry_hash` of the entry before it, and the chain head after an entry is that entry's `entry_hash`. A retained chain MUST give each ContextEntry a distinct `entry_id` within the session, as the pinned ContextEntry schema specifies. A repeated identifier maps to `ecl.rule.acs-decision-recorded.v1`. This does not require distinct `step_id` values: the pinned Instrument specification's section 9.1 assigns an `intent_extension` the originating ASK's `step_id`.

The ACS session chain MUST be treated as a native record that coexists with EBMP-2 evidence under EBMP2-045: the signed ECL evidence bundle is the record of release, an ACS chain or chain head that disagrees with the ECL evidence MUST be reported as an integrity finding and MUST NOT be repaired by rewriting either record, and an ACS-Core signature (HMAC-SHA256 under a shared key) MUST NOT be presented as satisfying FR-108.

An adapter that retains exchange records for this profile MUST write each one as `ecl_acs_exchange_v1`, valid against `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/binding/acs-exchange/1`, and every value of `ecl.ext.acs-decision.v1` it emits MUST validate against `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/extension/acs-decision/1`. An exchange with `guardian.status` equal to `decided` MUST retain its `guardian.result`; the record verifier MUST report an absent result with `ecl.rule.acs-decision-recorded.v1`. A schema-gated verifier rejects that incomplete record with `ecl.error.schema-invalid.v1` before semantic checks.

requirements.text:
A deployment MUST publish the binding's exact capability table with each capability supported, native or unsupported, in which outcome-hold, outcome-challenge, obligations, validity-window, use-policy, safe-state, control-cancel, control-revoke, control-supersede, control-quarantine and control-halt MUST be native responsibilities of ECL.

The following capability dispositions form part of the binding. A deployment publishes this table with its implementation evidence.

`supported` means that the binding sends or consumes the capability. `native` means that the ECL protocol assigns the capability to ECL's own path, which the PDP cannot override; the disposition assigns that responsibility and does not claim that a deployment implements every native control operation. `unsupported` means that the binding neither sends the capability nor treats it as a release capability, so a request or response that depends on it is refused or not produced. A deployment publishes this table, with these dispositions, under AZB1-006.

| Capability | Disposition | ECL behavior |
|---|---|---|
| evaluation | supported | One evaluation per decision attempt. |
| decision-boolean | supported | Only unqualified boolean true contributes to admit. |
| request-correlation | supported | Fresh request id and unpooled connection; echo recorded only. |
| evaluations-batch | unsupported | No batch endpoint; an empty evaluations array could evaluate defaults under AuthZEN §7.1. |
| metadata-discovery | unsupported | Evaluation URL is pinned configuration. |
| search-subject | unsupported | No search endpoint. |
| search-resource | unsupported | No search endpoint. |
| search-action | unsupported | No search endpoint. |
| decision-context | unsupported | A context-qualified permit denies; context is never interpreted as an obligation. |
| signed-metadata | unsupported | No signed PDP metadata is accepted. |
| policy-reference | unsupported | The PDP supplies no ECL policy identifier, version or digest. The DCMP-2 response binds the policy that the decision point applied (DCMP2-016); the digests of the PDP request and response and the PDP endpoint identify the exchange. |
| outcome-hold | native | A boolean PDP cannot originate a DCMP-2 hold. |
| outcome-challenge | native | A boolean PDP cannot originate a DCMP-2 challenge. |
| obligations | native | ECL must handle obligations; PDP context never creates one. |
| validity-window | native | ECL must set and check the authority window. |
| use-policy | native | The ECL decision and enforcement path must own use charges and quota. |
| safe-state | native | A dependency-failure deny must apply ECL's declared safe-state rule (DCMP2-041). |

Running and these terminal states record an execution attempt after release; a refusal or expiry before release uses its non-execution state. requirements.text: An observation MUST be an EBMP-2 `verification` event; a verifier MUST report one that is not with `ecl.error.semantic-invalid.v1`. A verifier MUST evaluate every envelope under TRUST-POLICY-1: historical validity at the object's own time under the policy version the object names, and current status at the evaluation time under the caller's current policy. The object's purpose is the one that INTEGRITY-ENVELOPE-1 IE1-039 gives its role: the decision-request purpose for a decision request, the decision-response purpose for a decision response, the evidence-event purpose for an EBMP-2 event in `envelopes` and the observation purpose for one in `observations`. The object's own time is its `issued_at` for DCMP-2 and its `observed_at` for EBMP-2, and its signed verification-time policy MUST be `ecl.time.issued-at.v1` and `ecl.time.observed-at.v1` respectively, which IE1-040 step 4 checks; when every trusted-time countersignature of the envelope is valid (IE1-032 to IE1-036), each signature that a countersignature covers is evaluated at the earliest attested time among those that cover it, in place of the object's own time, and each other signature at the object's own time (IE1-034). An envelope whose object has no such purpose, no own time or no supplied policy version (TP1-001) is not historically valid, with `ecl.error.signature-policy-invalid.v1`. Otherwise every signer of the envelope MUST pass IE1-040 step 6 (a) to (c) under the object's purpose and principal (TP1-004, TP1-005), and the envelope's status is then the code of IE1-040. An object of the bundle, in `envelopes` or `observations`, whose own time, or the attested time of one of its trusted-time countersignatures, is later than the evaluation time is not historically valid, with `ecl.error.clock-regressed.v1`: evidence cannot be later than the instant at which it is verified.

Two requests with one identity or one action attempt, two responses to one request, an authority event without a unique response, or an event without a request MUST make the bundle invalid, and a verifier MUST report each with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`.

requirements.text: A verifier MUST apply DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-051 to every request and response pair, EBMP2-046 to EBMP2-056, EBMP2-070 and EBMP2-072 to EBMP2-075 to every event, and the causal rules of section 4, EBMP2-077 among them, to every object that the bundle holds: each DCMP-2 message and EBMP-2 event in `envelopes` and each observation. Each object's causal predecessors MUST be objects of the bundle, with digests equal to the predecessor references; a signed evidence bundle declares no external dependency (EBMP2-023), so a predecessor that it does not hold, a DCMP-2 message of a type that the bundle does not carry included, is unresolved. Identifiers are unique across `envelopes` and `observations`: a DCMP-2 message is identified by its `message_id` and an EBMP-2 record by its `object_id`. An object that a causal predecessor reference or `continues` names and that the bundle does not hold exempts no other check: a verifier runs every check whose objects the bundle holds, and a failure of such a check gives its finding and verdict as if nothing were absent; the absent object makes the causal closure incomplete and keeps out of `established` every item whose object set names it (EBMP2-076). A proof that EBMP2-070 lets a discharge entry reference without carrying it is not such an object: it keeps `prerelease-obligations-proofs-verified` out of `established`, with the reason that the table gives, and changes no verdict. Registry snapshots and policy references are not objects of the causal graph.

requirements.text: A verifier MUST report exactly one verdict: `invalid` when an object of the bundle, in `envelopes` or `observations`, is not historically valid, a trust dependency of it among the reasons (TRUST-POLICY-1 TP1-006), an object fails its schema or semantic rules, a pairing, binding, outcome-reason or causal rule fails, or causal analysis is indeterminate; `incomplete` when causal closure is incomplete or a request has no terminal event; `current-trust-failed` when the bundle would otherwise be `verified` but some trust dependency, a time authority's key included, is revoked, expired or otherwise not acceptable under the current policy at the evaluation time; and `verified` otherwise. A verifier MUST NOT report `verified` for a bundle with a current trust failure unless its caller has explicitly accepted current trust failures for that run, and then MUST report the acceptance with the verdict. The acceptance applies to the `current-trust-failed` verdict only: it never changes an `invalid` or `incomplete` verdict, so it cannot restore evidence that is not historically valid. The primary finding of an `invalid` bundle is the one EBMP2-068 gives, that of an `incomplete` bundle is `ecl.error.causal-closure-incomplete.v1`, and that of a `current-trust-failed` bundle is the current status of its trust dependencies that comes first in the order of stage 4 of EBMP2-068.

requirements.text: A verifier MUST report the evidence level of each terminal effect: `none` when the terminal is not historically valid; `issuer-asserted` when it is; and `corroborated` only when the terminal state is `succeeded`, the terminal lists at least one side effect, the report establishes `envelope-signatures` and `causal-completeness` (EBMP2-076), and every listed side effect has an observation that is a historically valid `verification` event with decision `pass` whose `subject` has the side effect's `uri` and digest, that names the terminal event among its causal predecessors by `object_id` and digest, that has the terminal's `workflow.workflow_id`, `workflow.root_trace_id` and `workflow.attempt`, observed no earlier than the terminal, produced by a principal other than the terminal's producer, and signed only with key material disjoint from the terminal's. Corroboration therefore binds one observation to one terminal event of one attempt.

requirements.text: A verifier MUST declare finite limits on the number of envelopes and observations and on the decoded payload nodes of a bundle, MUST count the nodes of each payload while it parses it, against those that remain of the bundle's limit, so that it builds no payload beyond that limit (IE1-029), and MUST refuse a bundle that exceeds them before verifying signatures, with `ecl.error.resource-limit-exceeded.v1`. For example, a verifier can declare limits of 256 envelopes, 256 observations and 100 000 nodes.

A human intervention event that approves or rejects and carries `ecl.ext.approval-record.v1` MUST have an `issued_at` no earlier than `presented_at` plus `minimum_review_seconds`. A consumer MUST reject one that does not with `ecl.rule.approval-review-time-respected.v1`.

An event that carries `ecl.ext.control-change.v1` MUST name at least one approver, none of whom is the requester, and a change of kind `disable`, `bypass` or `auto_approve` MUST carry an `expires_at` later than its `effective_at`. A consumer MUST reject an event that does not with `ecl.rule.control-change-approved-and-bounded.v1`.

The execution events of one attempt, those with the same `event.action_id` and `event.attempt_id`, taken in ascending order of `workflow.sequence` and then of `object_id`, MUST carry states in which every state after the first is one that the table lists for the state before it. A consumer MUST reject a bundle with an attempt that does not with `ecl.rule.execution-state-transition-valid.v1`.

The states of one attempt move only forward along the progression above. This table gives, for each state, the states that may follow it in the same attempt; an attempt's first state may be any state, and nothing follows a terminal outcome or a non-execution terminal disposition.

| State | States that may follow it |
|---|---|
| `not_started` | `prepared`, `denied`, `held`, `challenged`, `expired_before_release` |
| `prepared` | `released`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `denied`, `held`, `challenged`, `expired_before_release` |
| `released` | `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `partially_succeeded`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `unknown` |
| `running` | `succeeded`, `failed`, `partially_succeeded`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `rolled_back`, `compensated`, `unknown` |

Every execution event with the same `event.action_id`, `workflow.workflow_id` and `workflow.attempt` MUST carry the same `event.attempt_id`, and one `event.attempt_id` MUST NOT appear with two different such triples. A bundle verifier MUST report a bundle that breaks this as invalid with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`.

requirements.text: A verifier MUST apply the verification profile that its caller names, and the reference verification profile `ecl.verification-profile.reference.v1` when the caller names none; a bundle does not select its profile. The verifier MUST report the profile it applied with the verdict. The registered reference profiles use zero response clock skew. A verifier MUST refuse a nonzero `response_clock_skew_seconds` input for one of those profiles rather than report a reference-profile result under different time rules. Every report MUST state the effective `response_clock_skew_seconds`.

A native adapter binding (`ecl_adapter_binding_v1`) binds one retained implementation-native object to the ECL objects derived from it. A consumer MUST reject a binding with `ecl.rule.adapter-source-binding-valid.v1` unless each of the following conditions holds:

1. `binding_digest` is the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the restricted
   canonical JSON of the binding without its `binding_digest` member.
2. `binding_id` is `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/adapter-binding/sha256/`
   followed by the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the restricted
   canonical JSON of an object with exactly five members: `system`, `contract`
   and `object_id`, each equal to that member of `source`; `object_digest`,
   equal to `source.object_digest.value`; and `ecl_object_ids`, the `object_id`
   of each `ecl_objects` entry, in order.
3. No two `ecl_objects` entries have the same `object_id`.
4. Each `ecl_objects` entry has the `protocol` `DCMP-2` and the `media_type`
   `application/vnd.ecl.dcmp+json`, or the `protocol` `EBMP-2` and the
   `media_type` `application/vnd.ecl.ebmp+json`.
5. No two `field_accounting` entries have the same `source_path`.
6. `loss_class` is `rejected` when the `disposition` of some `field_accounting`
   entry is `rejected`, otherwise `loss_accounted` when the `disposition` of
   some entry is `retained_source_only`, and otherwise `lossless`.
7. Each item of the `target_paths` of a `field_accounting` entry, and the
   `target_path` of each `derived_fields` entry, is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901)
   whose first reference token is an array index in the sense of RFC 6901,
   section 4, less than the number of `ecl_objects` entries.
8. For each of the six responsibilities, its member of
   `responsibility_coverage` has the `status` `represented` exactly when some
   `ecl_objects` entry lists the responsibility in its `responsibilities`, and
   its `object_ids` are the `object_id` of each such entry, in the order of
   `ecl_objects`.
9. `authority_boundary` equals the one value that the schema allows for it.

evidence_obligations: verification reports for discharges whose proofs are carried, uncarried, unsigned, signed by another principal, of another type, bound to another exchange or stale at the release, from each verifier that the claim relies on
requirements.text:
When the decision response that an `execution_released` event records carries an obligation whose `satisfaction` is `before_release`, or carries in `ecl.ext.consequence-coupling.v1` a `witness_result` whose `outcome` is `required_before_release`, the event MUST carry `ecl.ext.obligation-discharge.v1` with an entry for each such obligation: for an obligation, an entry whose `obligation_id` and `type` are the obligation's `id` and `type`; for the witness result, one whose `obligation_id` is the `uri` of the result's `reference` and whose `type` is `ecl.obligation.verify-witness.v1`. Each entry MUST record the `result` `satisfied`, the proof that Enforcement checked by `reference` and by the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the proof's RFC 8785 canonical form, the proof's `issuer`, when the proof was obtained (`obtained_at`), when Enforcement checked it (`checked_at`) and, whenever the proof's type declares a freshness bound, `fresh_until`, the instant after which the proof no longer shows the obligation met, which MUST NOT be later than the bound that the proof declares. The obligations that need an entry are those of the signed response that the bundle holds and that EBMP2-058 pairs with the event, never a list that the producer states elsewhere. When the proof is an ECL object, a signed envelope of a registered type, the entry MUST carry it: the object that `reference` names by its `message_id` or `object_id` is in the bundle as its own object, a `verification` event among the `observations` and any other object among the `envelopes`, and `digest` is that object's digest; a proof that is not an ECL object is recorded by `kind`, `reference` and `digest` only. The table after this rule gives, for each obligation type, the object admitted as its proof, the member that binds the proof to the exchange and the issuer that the decision names for it. For an `execution_released` event that binds its request and response (section 10), a verifier MUST report `ecl.rule.prerelease-obligations-discharged.v1` when the extension or an entry for a required obligation is missing, or an entry exhibits defect 1, 2, 3, 4, or 6 below. It MUST report `ecl.error.obligation-unproven.v1` for defect 5, 7, or 8. These are the entry defects, subject to the checks and gates described after the table:

1. names an obligation that the response does not carry, or one that another
   entry also names;
2. records a `result` other than `satisfied`;
3. has a `checked_at` later than the event's `observed_at`, or earlier than the
   response's `issued_at` by more than the response clock-skew allowance of
   DCMP2-047;
4. has a proof whose `obtained_at` is later than the entry's `checked_at`;
5. carries a proof whose signers, as the trust policy binds their keys to
   principals, are not exactly the issuer that the decision names for the
   obligation, compared as exact strings with no decoding and no
   normalization, or any of whose signing keys the trust policy binds to the
   requesting actor, or, for an approval obligation, carries an approval
   record whose signing keys do not all hold `ecl.purpose.approval.v1` in the
   trust-policy version that the record names; the entry's `issuer` is a
   label and is not the test;
6. names as its proof the `message_id` or `object_id` of an object in the
   bundle and gives a `digest` that is not that object's digest;
7. has a `fresh_until` that is not later than the event's `observed_at` plus
   its `release_guard_ms`, or carries a proof that declares a bound of its own,
   an approval record's `expires_at`, that is not later than the event's
   `observed_at` plus its `release_guard_ms`, whether or not the entry records
   `fresh_until`, or has a `fresh_until` later than that bound; or
8. carries a proof that is not a valid envelope under the trust policy, whose
   object type is not one that the obligation's type admits by the table, or
   that does not bind this exchange by the member that the table gives.

| Obligation type | Object admitted as its proof | Member that binds the proof to the exchange | Issuer that the decision names |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ecl.obligation.approval-record.v1` | A `human_intervention` event whose `operation` is `approve` and whose `actor` is the `approver` of the obligation's value | `target_id` equals the decision request's `message_id`, and one of its `causal_predecessors` names the request by `message_id` and digest | None: the approver is the record's actor, not its signer; in its place, every key that signed the record holds `ecl.purpose.approval.v1`, the purpose of an approval service |
| `ecl.obligation.verify-witness.v1`, a deferred witness result included | A `verification` event whose `decision` is `pass` and whose `subject.uri` is the witness | One of its `causal_predecessors` names the decision request by `message_id` and digest | The `source` of the witness result, when the response gives one; otherwise the decision names none |
| Any other type | Any EBMP-2 event record; a decision request or a decision response is never a proof | One of its `causal_predecessors` names the decision request by `message_id` and digest | None |

These checks belong to stage 8 of EBMP2-068 and read the members that are present with the types their value schema gives them (DCMP2-043). An entry with defect 1 is not checked further. The result and time checks in 2 to 4, and the entry's own `fresh_until` check in 7, apply to every remaining entry. Checks 5, 6, and 8 apply only to a proof carried in the bundle. A carried proof's digest mismatch (6) prevents checks 5 and 8 and the carried-proof freshness checks in 7 from using that mismatched object. The entry's own `fresh_until` check still applies whether or not the proof is carried. A verifier does not check the digest, the signer or the type of a proof held elsewhere, and does not tell from an uncarried proof's `kind` whether it is an ECL object. Where the decision names no issuer for an obligation, a witness result without `source` or an obligation of a type for which the table names none, the issuer test of condition 5 is not made, its other tests stand, and the scope item `prerelease-obligations-proofs-verified` is not established, with the reason `issuer-not-named` (EBMP2-076); for an approval obligation the approval purpose stands for the issuer. A discharge is the enforcement point's statement. A verifier that finds the record complete has checked that it names every obligation that the response leaves to Enforcement and that it agrees with the rest of the bundle, and, for a proof that the bundle carries, the proof's signatures, issuer, type, binding and freshness; it has not checked that a proof establishes what the obligation requires, or that the obligation was met, and its report says so (EBMP2-076).

evidence_obligations: fault-injection results that delay each operation that can block between the decision and the release
sampled execution_released and execution_terminal events with their recorded times
the declared release guard and the release_guard_ms that each execution_released event records
the enforcement point's declared release boundary and the code path from the decision to the release
requirements.text: The `observed_at` of an `execution_released` event MUST be the enforcement point's observation of the release boundary that its profile declares, taken after every operation that can block or wait between the decision and the release, such as writing the evidence of the consumed authority, waiting for a lock or obtaining the proof of an obligation, other than the recording of the `execution_released` event itself and the steps that the enforcement point's profile bounds by a declared release guard; the event MUST carry that guard as `release_guard_ms`, an integer number of milliseconds from 1 to 60000, the declared bound on the delay from the observation to the release, within which the release begins. It MUST NOT be an earlier time, such as the time at which the event was built, the response was received or the authority was consumed, when such an operation comes between that time and the release. An enforcement point that observes, by its own clock immediately after the release, that the authorization's `valid_until` had passed before the release completed MUST record that in the terminal event of the attempt, in an extension that it marks critical (XR1-005), and MUST NOT take that observation from the time at which the point of effect answered. EBMP2-050 and EBMP2-072 compare these times with the authorization's validity window. A recorded time is the producer's statement (EBMP2-004): no verifier establishes from the evidence alone that it is the true time of the event.

A verifier MUST report with `ecl.error.expired.v1`, as a finding of stage 7 of EBMP2-068, an `execution_terminal` event that binds its request and response and carries `ecl.ext.mcp-binding.v1` with `released_after_valid_until` set to `true`, whatever the extension's `critical` member says: the enforcement point states that its release may have come after `valid_until`. A `forward_completed_at` at or after `valid_until` is not a finding, since the answer to a request released inside its window can arrive after the authority has expired; a verifier MUST report such a completion beside the scope of its verdict as `completion_after_window` set to `true` (EBMP2-076). The terminal event's own `observed_at` is not compared with the window, since an effect can end after its authority has expired.

An `authority_consumed` event in state `consumed` that binds its response under EBMP2-052 MUST refer to a `single_use` authorization whose `max_uses` is absent or the integer 1. If the event carries `use_count`, it MUST be the integer 1. A bundle MUST NOT hold, for one authorization, more than one `authority_consumed` event in state `consumed` that binds its response under EBMP2-052, whether or not the event carries `use_count`. A verifier MUST report a bundle that breaks this with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`, as a finding of stage 7 of EBMP2-068. An unsupported authorization policy MUST NOT be interpreted as an unlimited use count.

An action attempt with an `execution_released` event that binds its request and response MUST also have an `authority_consumed` event in state `consumed` (EBMP2-008), whatever its terminal state. A verifier MUST apply this rule to every such attempt, whatever the causal closure of the rest of the bundle, except an attempt one of whose objects in the bundle names a causal predecessor that the bundle does not hold, since that predecessor could be the consumption (EBMP2-059). A verifier MUST report an attempt that does not with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`, as a finding of stage 8 of EBMP2-068.

When a request carries `ecl.ext.mcp-binding.v1`, a `release_prepared`, `execution_released`, `execution_observed` or `execution_terminal` event of its action that carries the extension MUST carry, in each occurrence, every member of the request's value with the same value, so that the evidence names the call that was decided; and an `execution_terminal` event in state `succeeded` or `failed` MUST carry the extension with `response_digest`, the digest of the server's response. A verifier MUST report an event that binds its request and response and breaks this with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`, as a finding of stage 7 of EBMP2-068. The request's value is that of its first occurrence of the extension.

evidence_obligations: verification reports, in their machine-readable and text forms, with the scope of each verdict
requirements.text:
With each verdict a verifier MUST report its scope, as the two lists of the table below: `established`, the checks that it made for the bundle and that held, and `not_established`, the other checks that apply to the bundle and the statements that no verification establishes, each list in the order of the table. Where the table names a reason for which an item is not established, the report MUST give that reason with the item. A report whose verdict is `invalid`, or in which no envelope was evaluated, MUST have an empty `established`. A verifier MUST NOT list in `established` a check that it did not make or that failed, and wherever it shows a verdict to a person it MUST show the `not_established` list with it. The registry `registries/scope-checks.json` (schema `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/scope-checks/1`) gives, for each item of the table and for the `corroborated` evidence level of EBMP2-061, its object set, the checks that must hold over it, the trust knowledge they use and the waivers that it permits. A waiver changes the verdict only (EBMP2-060): an item whose failure the waiver accepts stays in `not_established`, and no item is ever established over less than its whole object set. A verifier MUST NOT list an item in `established` unless it ran every check that the registry requires for the item over the item's whole object set and each held, a check with nothing to check in that set holding; MUST NOT list an item in `established` when its object set names an object that the bundle does not hold, whatever the verdict; MUST NOT report the `corroborated` level unless every check and item that the registry requires for it held; and MUST report, for each item in `established`, the checks that it ran for the item and the objects that they covered. Every report MUST state, in the member `evaluation_time`, the evaluation time that it used, and every report MUST carry the member `unresolved_predecessor_ids`, the identifiers of the predecessors that it could not resolve, which is non-empty only when the verdict is `incomplete`. A report MUST carry, beside the scope, the informational member `completion_after_window` set to `true` when a terminal event records a `forward_completed_at` at or after the authorization's `valid_until` (EBMP2-072); the member is not a finding and changes no verdict. An offline package has the scope of the report that IE1-022 gives it.

The qualifying verdicts used below are `verified`, `current-trust-failed` and `incomplete`. A qualifying verdict is necessary but is not sufficient: each item must also pass every check on its complete object set in the scope-check registry. Object-signing dependencies and time-attestation-signing dependencies are distinct sets. All signatures on a time attestation must meet the historical eligibility and revocation checks for `trusted-time` to be established, including signatures not needed to meet its threshold. A valid threshold alone does not establish that scope item. `current-trust` includes both dependency sets.

| Item | What it says | When it is established |
|---|---|---|
| `envelope-signatures` | Each envelope's and observation's payload digest and signatures verify under the trust-policy version that its object names, at the object's own time or its trusted time, and the caller's current policy revokes none of its object-signing dependencies at or before its time (EBMP2-057, TRUST-POLICY-1 TP1-006). | A qualifying verdict and every required registry check over the complete object-signing dependency set. |
| `current-trust` | Each trust dependency, each signing key of each envelope and observation and of each time attestation, is acceptable under the caller's current trust policy at the evaluation time (EBMP2-060, TRUST-POLICY-1 TP1-006). | The verdict is `verified` or `incomplete` and every trust dependency's current status is valid; an acceptance of current trust failures never establishes it. |
| `trusted-time` | A separate time authority attests a time for each signature of each envelope and observation, binding that signature (IE1-033), and each signature was valid at that time (IE1-032 to IE1-035); each time authority's key is valid at its attested time under the policy version its attestation names and is not revoked by the caller's current policy at or before that time (TRUST-POLICY-1 TP1-006). | A qualifying verdict and every required registry check over the item's complete object set, and every signature of every envelope and observation is covered by a valid trusted-time countersignature. |
| `object-rules` | Each signed object satisfies its schema and its semantic rules, the one-way rule for a recorded decision basis among them (EBMP2-068, stage 3). | A qualifying verdict and every required registry check over the item's complete object set. |
| `decision-basis-recorded` | Each decision response records its decision basis (DCMP2-053). | A qualifying verdict and every required registry check over the item's complete object set. |
| `decision-basis-register` | Each decision basis names the supplied register version and matches its declared inputs, classes, required flags, sources and derivations. Recorded input timing is compared with declared deadlines and maximum ages only when the necessary fields are supplied (DCMP2-053). This check does not re-evaluate policy or approval thresholds. | A qualifying verdict and every required registry check over the item's complete object set. It applies only when the caller supplies a register. |
| `decision-input-timing` | The recorded ages and acquisition times of every available input with a declared temporal constraint meet the supplied register's maximum ages and deadlines. This does not establish that any recorded time is true. | Applies only when a register is supplied and at least one available input has a declared maximum age or deadline. Established only with a qualifying verdict, every required registry check over the decision responses, and all operands needed for those comparisons present; otherwise not established, with `input-times-not-recorded` when a needed timestamp is absent or unreadable. Unavailable, late or malformed inputs create no available-input timing check. |
| `bindings` | Each response binds its request, each event binds its request, response and authority, with the digests and use counts that they name, each continuation binds the request, challenge and approval that it continues, and each terminal event carries the outcome reason that its state and response require (DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-051, EBMP2-047 to EBMP2-054, EBMP2-056, EBMP2-073, EBMP2-075, EBMP2-078). | A qualifying verdict and every required registry check over the item's complete object set. |
| `release-within-authority` | Each recorded release time lies within the authorization's validity window with the release guard added, and no terminal event records that a release may have come after `valid_until` (EBMP2-050, EBMP2-072). | A qualifying verdict and every required registry check over the item's complete object set, when the bundle records a release; when it records none, it is not established, with the reason `no-release-recorded`. |
| `causal-completeness` | Over every object that the bundle holds, the DCMP-2 messages and EBMP-2 events in `envelopes` and the observations: every causal predecessor is in the bundle with the digest that names it, in the workflow, trace and attempt that EBMP2-077 allows, the graph is acyclic and identifiers are unique, and every request has a terminal event (section 4, EBMP2-055, EBMP2-059, EBMP2-074, EBMP2-077). | The verdict is `verified` or `current-trust-failed`. |
| `prerelease-obligations-discharge-recorded` | Each release records a discharge of every obligation that its decision left to Enforcement before the release, checked no later than the release was observed and fresh at the release (EBMP2-070). | A qualifying verdict and every required registry check over the item's complete object set. It applies only when the verifier applied EBMP2-070 to an `execution_released` event whose response carries such an obligation. |
| `prerelease-obligations-proofs-verified` | Each pre-release discharge carries its proof, and each proof is a valid ECL object under the trust policy, signed by the issuer the obligation names, of a type the obligation admits, bound to this exchange and fresh at the release (EBMP2-070). | As `prerelease-obligations-discharge-recorded`, and only when every entry's proof is an ECL object that the bundle carries and that passes conditions 5, 7 and 8 of EBMP2-070, with the discharge checks (including condition 6) already satisfied; when an entry's proof is not an ECL object that the bundle carries, it is not established, with the reason `proof-not-ecl-object`, and when the decision names no issuer for an obligation, with the reason `issuer-not-named`; when both apply, the report gives `proof-not-ecl-object`. |
| `prerelease-obligations-met` | That each pre-release obligation was met: the verifier checks a proof's signatures, issuer, type, binding and freshness, not what the proof shows. | Never; it applies as `prerelease-obligations-discharge-recorded` does. |
| `post-release-obligations-met` | That the obligations to be met during or after execution were met, which the verifier does not check. | Never; it applies only when the response that an `execution_released` event records carries an obligation whose `satisfaction` is `during_execution` or `after_execution`. |
| `recorded-times-true` | That each recorded time is the true time of its event: each producer states its own times (EBMP2-004, EBMP2-071). | Never. |
| `effects-occurred` | That the effects happened: a terminal event is its producer's statement, and corroboration is another signed statement, an observation bound to that terminal event and its attempt (EBMP2-015, EBMP2-061). | Never. |
| `deployment-assessed` | That the deployment that produced the evidence has been assessed or meets ECL-1. | Never. |
| `statements-true` | That the statements in the bundle are true (section 1), among them the enforcement point's statements of what it checked and released. | Never. |

requirements.text:
A causal predecessor MUST have its successor's `workflow.root_trace_id`, and MUST be in its successor's workflow, in the workflow that its successor's `workflow.parent_workflow_id` names, or in a child workflow whose own `workflow.parent_workflow_id` names the successor's workflow. The last case permits a parent to join its child's recorded result (DW1-002, DW1-009); it does not permit a reference to an unrelated or sibling workflow. For a child-to-parent join, the child record MUST have a causal path to the exact creating or delegating object in its declared parent workflow. The path consists of zero or more predecessor edges within the child workflow, followed by a predecessor edge to that parent object. Every edge MUST bind the predecessor's logical identifier and canonical digest; every child record on the path MUST identify the same parent and root trace. A declared parent identifier alone does not establish this relationship. Held ancestors in that child workflow MUST agree on its declared parent, including when another predecessor is absent.

If no such path exists in the held graph and no named absent predecessor could complete it, the verifier MUST report `ecl.rule.bundle-causal-context-consistent.v1`. When no held path establishes the origin, a named absent predecessor on a possible path leaves it unresolved and MUST prevent causal-completeness scope, including when that predecessor is declared external. A later child record can inherit its origin through earlier child records; it need not repeat the direct reference to the parent object.

A predecessor in its successor's workflow MUST NOT have a greater `workflow.attempt` than its successor: a later attempt can follow an earlier one, never the reverse. A verifier MUST report a predecessor that the bundle holds and that fails this rule with `ecl.rule.bundle-causal-context-consistent.v1`. Sequence and attempt counters in different workflows are separate domains; neither counter supplies a global order. Digest resolution, acyclicity and required-child closure still apply. An absent child record leaves a required join unresolved, rather than establishing the child's completion.

requirements.text: A bundle MAY hold a continued request and its continuation (DCMP-2 DCMP2-056), each with its own response and attempt, and then verifies as one history. For a request that carries `continues`, a verifier MUST check that the bundle's objects that `continues` names are the decision request that `request_id` names; the decision response that `response_id` names, whose `request_id` is that request's `message_id` and whose `outcome` is `challenge`; and the `human_intervention` event that `approval_id` names, whose `operation` is `approve` and whose `target_id` is the continued request's `message_id`; that the continuation's workflow, attempt, `action`, `actor`, `subject` and `authority_request` relate to the continued request's as DCMP2-056 requires; that the continuation lists the response and the approval that `continues` names among its `workflow.causal_predecessors`, each by identifier and digest; and that no two requests of the bundle which continue the same response have decision responses whose `outcome` is `admit`. A continuation answered with `deny` or `challenge` does not violate this uniqueness condition; its remaining binding and causal checks still apply. When the continuation's response is an `admit`, the verifier MUST also check that every key that signed the approval holds `ecl.purpose.approval.v1` in the trust-policy version that the approval names, and that no key that signed it is bound to the request's actor, as EBMP2-070 condition 5 asks of an approval record; and that the approval's required `expires_at` is later than the `evaluated_at` of that response. A continuation answered with a `deny` or a new `challenge`, as DCMP2-057 requires for an approval that is late, expired or not acceptable, is correct evidence and is not refused for its approval. A verifier MUST report a continuation that fails a check with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`, as a finding of stage 5 of EBMP2-068. A named object that the bundle does not hold leaves the causal closure incomplete (EBMP2-059) and keeps `bindings` out of `established` (EBMP2-076); it exempts no other check of this rule.

The minimum independence class for a claim is defined in Section 7. `Class A` is same-operator separation only. It is not the same thing as separate administration or external independence and MUST NOT be represented as satisfying those stronger properties. At every class, a claim MUST give a capability matrix for the governed AI, ordinary operators, administrators, credential and key custodians, and host or hypervisor roots. It MUST state which powers can alter each plane, which changes require separate credentials or authorities, and what host compromise defeats. Co-location MUST NOT be used as an exception to FR-001: if one shared host root or administrative role can alter both AI behavior and effective in-scope control outcomes, no class is satisfied, even when ordinary runtime credentials differ. Separate process names, audit logs or keys that the shared root can read or replace do not establish separation. Soft enforcement by itself does not establish FR-001.

| Class | Operator and administration | Single-power and host-compromise test | Additional boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | One operator can administer both planes through separated powers | No one credential, role, privilege domain or trust root can alter both planes; co-hosting is acceptable only when this remains true | Same-operator separation, without a claim of separate administration |
| B | Both control approval and evidence verification have separately administered domains | Every Class A single-power test passes; the AI and its ordinary operators cannot change either function | Both functions are separately administered, including their change authority |
| C | Every Class B condition holds and both functions are externally held | Every Class B test passes and the SoI operator cannot unilaterally control either function | Both functions belong to an externally independent domain or authority |

evidence_obligations: evidence-signing key inventory, every trust-policy version in force during the assessment period, key-store configuration and export policy, signing-operation records, rotation records, the compromise-response procedure and the record of its last exercise, and for L3 and above the hardware attestations or validation certificates, for L4 the key-ceremony records
requirements.text: When an evidence-signing key is known or suspected to be compromised, the claimant MUST publish a trust-policy version that revokes the key with an effective time no later than the earliest suspected time of compromise, MUST deliver that version to its verifiers within the connected revocation propagation bound of its declared timing case (Section 8.7), and MUST record the event, the revocation, and the evidence that the key signed between the effective time and the revocation's publication. The claimant MUST exercise this procedure at least once per assessment cycle. A verifier applies the revocation to every object and every time attestation that the key signed whose time, the object's own or attested time or the attestation's attested time, is at or after the revocation's effective time, whatever trust-policy version the object names.

requirements.text: For `L2` and above, each in-scope action class with financial, legal, data-disclosure, communication, identity, infrastructure, or physical consequence MUST be subject to at least one consequence budget that limits the aggregate count, rate, or value of its admitted actions over a declared period. The budget MUST be enforced outside the governed AI system, MUST count the actions of every session, workflow, and instance of the SoI, and MUST cause a `deny` or `hold` decision for any action that would exceed it.

evidence_obligations: Approval interface, approval records carrying ecl.ext.approval-record.v1, declared minimum review times, approval-rate and review-time monitoring, and decision samples for action classes with a human-approval threshold
requirements.text: When a person approves or rejects a consequential action, the approval or rejection MUST be made on a human-readable presentation of its operation, target, every parameter material to its consequences, the policy outcome and reasons, and the `verifiable` inputs on which the decision rested. A digest MUST NOT substitute for those fields. The presentation MUST show applicable amounts, units, currency, rounding, recipient or account identity, resource or deletion scope, audience and privilege changes without ambiguous labels or silent truncation; localization and accessible alternatives MUST preserve that meaning. The claim MUST declare the consequential fields for each action class and give the approver access to the complete parameters. The presentation MUST be bound to the canonical action released, and a change to its operation, target or consequential parameters MUST invalidate the approval and require a new presentation and approval before release. The evidence MUST record the approver, the presentation's reference and digest, its time, the bound action identity and digest, and the decision; the retained presentation MUST be available to the assessor subject to the retention procedure of ECL1N-0195 to ECL1N-0199.

evidence_obligations: Approval interface, approval records carrying ecl.ext.approval-record.v1, declared minimum review times, approval-rate and review-time monitoring, and decision samples for action classes with a human-approval threshold
requirements.text: For `L2` and above, a claim MUST declare a minimum review time for each action class that requires approval, and an approval recorded sooner than that time after its presentation MUST NOT release the action.

requirements.text: For `L3` and above, the claimant MUST measure, for each approver and action class, the approval rate and the review times, and MUST treat a declared anomaly, such as more consecutive approvals without a rejection than a declared limit or review times below the declared minimum, as a verification finding that triggers review of that approver's decisions.

requirements.text:
When the Consequential Action Register declares a human-approval threshold for an action class (ECL1N-0007), the Decision Layer MUST NOT return `admit` for an action whose measure is at or above the threshold's value until the approvals of as many distinct authorized persons as the threshold requires are recorded; until then it MUST return `hold` or `challenge`, or `deny` where its verifiable-only outcome or another requirement of this standard requires a `deny`.

The register declares the thresholds of an action class in the `human_approval_threshold` member of its entry, a list of one or more thresholds (`schemas/ecl-action-register-v1.schema.json`). Each threshold names what it compares in one of two ways: `parameter`, an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to a value in the request's `action.parameters`, or `measure`, a URI naming a measure that the deployment defines, such as a consequence dimension or a value computed from several parameters, whose definition is reviewed with the register (EA-20). It also gives the unit, the value at or above which an action needs approval, as a decimal string, and the number of distinct authorized persons whose approval it needs. An action is at or above a `parameter` threshold when the value at the pointer is a non-negative integer, or a string in the decimal form of `value`, that is at or above `value`, the two compared as exact decimals; when the pointer names no value, or names a value of any other form (including a negative number), the action counts as at or above the threshold. An action at or above several thresholds needs, for each of them, the approvals that it requires; one person's approval counts toward each threshold that it applies to.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with the class, the required or optional declaration and the derivations of each decision input, write-access configuration of the input sources, policy, decision responses carrying ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, failure-injection records for required and optional inputs, and consequence-budget ledger entries for requests that declare a budget debit
requirements.text: For each in-scope action class, the Consequential Action Register MUST declare, for each decision input that ECL1N-0164 requires it to state, its class as `verifiable`, `actor_supplied`, or `judgment` (Section 4.3), whether the action class requires it, its source, the maximum age of its value, and, when the Decision Layer must obtain it within a set time, its deadline: the time after the Decision Layer receives a request by which it must have the input. An input whose asserted value the governed AI system produces or can overwrite without independent validation, or whose authenticity or transition checks it can modify or bypass, MUST be declared `actor_supplied`; the output of a probabilistic model or heuristic detector about meaning or risk MUST NOT be declared `verifiable`. For each `verifiable` input the claim MUST identify the authority, its validation rules and the controls on freshness, selection and completeness on which an admit relies. An admitted action that causes an independently validated transition MUST NOT by that fact alone make the resulting authoritative observation `actor_supplied`. An actor's selection or omission of authentic observations MUST NOT establish completeness that neither the authority attests nor the Decision Layer independently establishes. An input that reaches the Decision Layer through the request, or through any channel that the governed AI system can write, MUST be declared `actor_supplied` unless the Decision Layer authenticates its origin as Section 4.3 requires. The Decision Layer MUST NOT consult a decision input that the register does not declare for the action class. The register MUST declare each action class once and each decision input of a class once. For an input that is computed from other declared inputs of the class, the register MUST name those inputs, MUST NOT declare the input `verifiable` unless each of them is `verifiable`, and MUST NOT declare it computed from itself, directly or through other inputs.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with the class, the required or optional declaration and the derivations of each decision input, write-access configuration of the input sources, policy, decision responses carrying ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, failure-injection records for required and optional inputs, and consequence-budget ledger entries for requests that declare a budget debit
requirements.text: An `actor_supplied` or `judgment` input MUST NOT be the basis of an `admit`. The outcome of a decision MUST be no less strict, in the strictness order of Section 4.3, than its verifiable-only outcome. Such an input MAY make the outcome stricter, including by bringing into effect a detection response declared under ECL1N-0167 and ECL1N-0168, and MUST NOT make it less strict, select an authorization wider than the verifiable-only outcome's, remove an obligation, reduce or defer a consequence-budget debit, or raise or remove a human-approval threshold or lower the number of distinct approvers it requires.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with the class, the required or optional declaration and the derivations of each decision input, write-access configuration of the input sources, policy, decision responses carrying ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, failure-injection records for required and optional inputs, and consequence-budget ledger entries for requests that declare a budget debit
requirements.text: An `admit` MUST be justified by policy evaluated over `verifiable` inputs alone: its verifiable-only outcome is `admit`, and its authorization is that outcome's authorization or stricter.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with the class, the required or optional declaration and the derivations of each decision input, write-access configuration of the input sources, policy, decision responses carrying ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, failure-injection records for required and optional inputs, and consequence-budget ledger entries for requests that declare a budget debit
requirements.text:
The evidence of each decision MUST identify, by reference and digest, the version of the Consequential Action Register under which the decision was made, and each decision input that the Decision Layer consulted and each that the register declares for the action class, each input once, with its declared class, whether the action class requires it, whether it was available, late, unavailable, or malformed, its reference and digest when it was available, and its effect on the outcome. The decision response MUST carry this record in the registered extension `ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1` (DCMP2-053). Effects are relative to the verifiable-only outcome of Section 4.3 and the authorization, obligations, consequence-budget debits, and human-approval requirements that accompany it:

- `supports`: the input is part of the basis on which the verifiable-only
  outcome permits the action, whatever the final outcome. An input that
  belongs to both the permitting and restricting bases MUST be recorded as
  `supports`;
- `restricts`: the input is part of the basis on which the verifiable-only
  outcome refuses or narrows the action, through a `verifiable` input's value
  or the absence of a required `verifiable` input; or it is part of the basis
  on which the final outcome is stricter than the verifiable-only outcome,
  through an `actor_supplied` or `judgment` input or an unavailable, late, or
  malformed optional input (ECL1N-0179, ECL1N-0182);
- `none`: the input is part of neither basis.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with the class, the required or optional declaration and the derivations of each decision input, write-access configuration of the input sources, policy, decision responses carrying ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, failure-injection records for required and optional inputs, and consequence-budget ledger entries for requests that declare a budget debit
requirements.text: A declared decision input is late when the Decision Layer obtains it after its declared deadline, or when its value is older than its declared maximum age at the time of the decision; it is unavailable when the Decision Layer does not obtain it before it decides, and malformed when it does not have its declared form or its integrity cannot be verified. An input that is unavailable, late, or malformed MUST NOT be part of the basis of an `admit`. If the register declares the input required for the action class, the outcome MUST NOT be `admit`; if the register declares it optional, the input MAY make the outcome stricter and MUST NOT otherwise affect it.
